## Why This Is Asked

Tests branchless bitwise selection across a 128-bit value. It mirrors practical use cases like compositing two 128-bit values with a mask in a single pass.

## Key Concepts

- Branchless bitwise selection
- 128-bit composition via hi/lo fields
- Handling of full-range masks across both lanes

## Code Example

```c
uint128 blend128(uint128 a, uint128 b, uint128 mask) {
  uint128 t1 = and128(a, mask);
  uint128 t2 = and128(b, not128(mask));
  return or128(t1, t2);
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you validate correctness across all 2^128 mask patterns efficiently?
- How would this approach extend to 256-bit operands with the same interface?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to manipulate multi-byte data with pure bitwise ops, a common low-level skill in performance-critical code.

## Key Concepts
- Byte masking with constants
- Shifts to relocate bytes
- Bitwise OR to assemble result
- No loops or branches; constant-time operation

```javascript
function swapBytes32(x) {
  return ((x & 0x000000FF) << 24) |
         ((x & 0x0000FF00) << 8)  |
         ((x & 0x00FF0000) >>> 8) |
         ((x & 0xFF000000) >>> 24);
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt for 64-bit values? 
- What edge cases arise in languages with signed shifts vs unsigned shifts?
